topic-152-a-case-study-in-the-use-of-the.evolution: The collection spans 1983–2026, but many early abstracts are unavailable, so a detailed methodological history is not supported. A recent tutoring position paper evaluates pressure from authority and face-saving requests, proposing supportive corrective behavior as an assessment target. This supplies a contemporary application of the theme, not proof of continuity with every archival method.
openQuestions: How can tutoring evaluations distinguish helpful encouragement from reinforcement of a misconception?
What evidence should trigger revision of an explicit theory rather than an ad hoc exception?
topic-152-a-case-study-in-the-use-of-the.overview: This cluster concerns learning through explicit knowledge, explanations, and revision of mistaken beliefs. Its archival titles emphasize explanation-based generalization, incomplete domain theories, and constructive induction. The available recent evidence addresses a practical counterpart: tutors must correct misconceptions rather than agree with a learner simply to appear supportive.
topic-152-a-case-study-in-the-use-of-the.title: Theory Revision and Corrective Explanation
topic-152-a-case-study-in-the-use-of-the.whyItMatters: Explanations are useful only if they can expose and repair errors. In educational interaction, social pressure can pull a model toward agreement even when the task requires a factual correction, making interpersonal style and epistemic reliability distinct objectives.

topic-153-v-0-a-generalist-value-model-f.evolution: The broader collection includes policy gradients for structured domains and memory-assisted program synthesis. Recent representatives focus on reasoning models, with offline value estimation, single-generation updates, prolonged training, and uncertainty-guided sample selection. These alternatives explore how much learning signal each trajectory supplies rather than assuming that more sampled answers always produce proportionate benefits.
openQuestions: Which sample-selection rules preserve difficult but important reasoning cases?
When can offline value estimates replace online exploration without limiting eventual capability?
topic-153-v-0-a-generalist-value-model-f.overview: This topic uses reinforcement learning to improve reasoning while reducing the cost of policy updates and generated trajectories. Methods change advantage estimation, sample selection, behavior preparation, and allocation of training or inference compute. The practical bottleneck is often repeated generation rather than the arithmetic of a parameter update.
topic-153-v-0-a-generalist-value-model-f.title: Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Language-Model Reasoning
topic-153-v-0-a-generalist-value-model-f.whyItMatters: Efficiency improvements can make reasoning training accessible, but fewer rollouts may reduce exploration or bias which problems receive attention. Accuracy, memory, generation cost, and robustness need to be evaluated together.

topic-154-1-norm-support-vector-machines.evolution: Early examples construct boundary-focused radial-basis models and simplify support-vector decisions. Later papers address kernel validity, efficient prediction, and optimal sparsity. Recent work revisits high-dimensional optimization and lets an SVM boundary guide deep feature updates. This broadens the use of margin geometry beyond a fixed final classifier without making classical and deep formulations identical.
openQuestions: How can sparse prediction retain useful margins under distribution shift?
When does joint feature–margin optimization improve over a strong fixed representation?
topic-154-1-norm-support-vector-machines.overview: Support vector methods organize classification around separating classes with a margin. The represented work studies sparse support sets, local linear models, indefinite kernels, scalable approximations, and connections to learned deep features. The classifier’s geometry and its computational representation are closely linked.
topic-154-1-norm-support-vector-machines.title: Margin-Based Learning and Support Vector Models
topic-154-1-norm-support-vector-machines.whyItMatters: A large support set can make prediction expensive even when training succeeds. At the same time, a margin is only useful in a feature space that captures relevant distinctions, motivating both theoretical bounds and joint representation learning.

topic-155-dynamic-knapsack-optimization-.evolution: The collection includes early advertising allocation and auction-price modeling. Later theory analyzes repeated posted prices and contextual mechanisms, while recent work handles budgeted first-price bidding and data as a continuously allocated digital good. These examples expand the market settings studied rather than establishing a universal auction rule.
openQuestions: Which learning guarantees survive strategic adaptation by multiple participants?
How should mechanisms balance data-production costs with uncertain future demand?
topic-155-dynamic-knapsack-optimization-.overview: Market learning involves prices, bids, budgets, and participants whose behavior changes in response to the mechanism. The represented work studies repeated auctions, strategic buyers, coordinated bidding, and selling data with diminishing returns. Unlike ordinary prediction, an algorithm’s decisions can alter the observations it later receives.
topic-155-dynamic-knapsack-optimization-.title: Learning in Auctions and Strategic Markets
topic-155-dynamic-knapsack-optimization-.whyItMatters: A good short-term price can undermine long-term learning when buyers act strategically. Budget and incentive constraints also change what regret or economic efficiency means, so guarantees must specify feedback and participant behavior.

topic-156-ell-1-regression-with-heavy-ta.evolution: Early representatives study uniform convergence and approximation. Later work estimates unseen mass and distributional properties, followed by heavy-tailed regression and assumption-light discrete-distribution learning. Recent mean-shift contamination analysis exploits structure that differs from arbitrary replacement noise. These models must remain distinct: robustness under one corruption mechanism does not automatically transfer to another.
openQuestions: Which observable diagnostics can justify a data-dependent estimation guarantee?
How much distributional structure is needed to recover information hidden by contamination?
topic-156-ell-1-regression-with-heavy-ta.overview: This topic asks how accurately a probability distribution, its mean, or one of its properties can be estimated from finite data. Sparse observations, infinite support, heavy tails, and contamination create different limits. The represented work combines algorithms with upper and lower bounds that clarify which assumptions make estimation possible.
topic-156-ell-1-regression-with-heavy-ta.title: Distribution Estimation and Robust Statistical Limits
topic-156-ell-1-regression-with-heavy-ta.whyItMatters: A precise estimate of the wrong quantity or an unsupported uniform guarantee can be misleading. Data-dependent bounds and explicit contamination models help connect theoretical accuracy to what the observed sample actually reveals.

topic-157-textits-sppo-semantic-calibrat.evolution: A 2016 representative connects task rewards with maximum-likelihood learning for structured outputs. More recent work develops direct preference optimization, explicit-reward alignment, and calibrated losses. The newest papers examine noise tolerance, representation-distance bias, and self-consuming data loops. This progression highlights feedback quality and objective design alongside computational simplicity.
openQuestions: Which preference-noise assumptions can be checked from real annotation data?
How should ties and legitimate disagreement influence alignment rather than be discarded?
topic-157-textits-sppo-semantic-calibrat.overview: Preference alignment adjusts language models using comparisons, rewards, or related supervision. The topic focuses on the mathematical objective: calibration, divergence choice, noise correction, and how ties or biased comparisons affect learning. A preference label is a measurement with uncertainty, not necessarily a clean statement of one universal utility.
topic-157-textits-sppo-semantic-calibrat.title: Preference Alignment Objectives and Noisy Feedback
topic-157-textits-sppo-semantic-calibrat.whyItMatters: Poorly modeled feedback can reward spurious distinctions or amplify annotation errors. Direct alignment objectives offer simpler training than online reinforcement learning, but their statistical meaning still depends on the assumed feedback process.

topic-158-de-randomized-smoothing-for-ce.evolution: Early work replaces Gaussian residual assumptions with heavy-tailed models. Later representatives study adversarial collective classification and multiple perturbation families. Recent theory sharpens nonparametric classification rates and examines sparse attacks on nonlinear systems. The shared development is more explicit control of uncertainty and disturbance structure, not a single defense applicable to every threat.
openQuestions: How can robustness guarantees be matched to realistic deployment disturbances?
When do stronger certificates impose unacceptable losses in ordinary predictive performance?
topic-158-de-randomized-smoothing-for-ce.overview: Robust learning limits the damage caused by outliers, malicious perturbations, or corrupted training and inference conditions. The represented papers span robust regression, adversarial classification, randomized smoothing, and dynamical-system identification. Each problem defines a different set of disturbances against which performance is assessed.
topic-158-de-randomized-smoothing-for-ce.title: Robust Learning and Adversarial Guarantees
topic-158-de-randomized-smoothing-for-ce.whyItMatters: A certificate is meaningful only relative to its perturbation model. Average-case accuracy, worst-case robustness, and probabilistic protection can conflict, so stronger language should not obscure assumptions about attack size, frequency, or distribution.

topic-159-mathcalo-log-n-latent-dimensio.evolution: The collection reaches back to 1987 connections between connectivity and problem complexity. Later results examine width, learning hardness, and depth separation. Recent analyses connect partial computation with accuracy and expose barriers inherited from circuit complexity. These results offer complementary limits rather than one scalar measure of neural capability.
openQuestions: Which expressivity advantages are reachable by practical optimization?
Can compute–accuracy guarantees remain informative for trained networks outside idealized asymptotic models?
topic-159-mathcalo-log-n-latent-dimensio.overview: Neural-network theory distinguishes which functions an architecture can represent, which can be learned efficiently, and which generalize from finite examples. Width, depth, weight magnitude, connectivity, and precision all enter these questions. The represented work also studies what approximation is lost when computation is pruned or stopped early.
topic-159-mathcalo-log-n-latent-dimensio.title: Neural Expressivity, Learnability, and Compute Bounds
topic-159-mathcalo-log-n-latent-dimensio.whyItMatters: A representation theorem alone does not explain successful training. Likewise, a smaller network may retain accuracy only for particular data geometry or parameter configurations. Sharp bounds help identify where architectural intuition is justified and where proof barriers remain.
